name: Tabs
description: The APG tabs pattern: one list of tabs over one panel at a time. Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/

props.name: children
props.description: The tabs and their panels: a `Tabs.List` of `Tabs.Tab`, then one `Tabs.Panel` per tab.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selection. Leave it out and the widget owns it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Which tab starts selected. Left out, nothing is selected and no panel is shown until one is chosen.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Fires with the newly selected tab and why it changed — `'click'` or `'keyboard'`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way the tabs run. Horizontal is the reading axis, so its arrows mirror in a right-to-left page.

props.name: activation
props.description: Whether moving to a tab selects it. Default `'automatic'`, which is what APG asks for.

props.name: loop
props.description: Whether the arrows wrap around at the ends. Default `true`.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Render every panel rather than only the selected one, hiding the rest. What a panel holding a half-filled form needs, since an unmounted panel loses its state.

parts.name: Tabs.List
parts.description: The tabs themselves, and the keyboard: it sits on the list because roving tabindex puts one tab in the tab sequence.

props.name: label
props.description: The list's accessible name. A tablist has none of its own, and one page can hold several.

props.name: labelledBy
props.description: Names the list after an element already on the page, instead of `label`.

parts.name: Tabs.Tab
parts.description: One tab: a real `<button>`, so Enter and Space reach it the way the platform means them to.

props.name: value
props.description: Which panel this tab shows, and what the widget reports when it is chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Not selectable, and stepped over by the arrows — unlike a disabled `Menu.Item`, which APG asks stay reachable. Selection follows focus here, so a tab focus could reach and selection could not would leave the widget with no state to be in.

parts.name: Tabs.Panel
parts.description: One panel. Rendered only while its tab is selected, unless the widget was told to keep them all.

props.name: value
props.description: The tab this panel belongs to.

keyboard.action: Enters the list once, landing on the selected tab, and again leaves it for the panel.
The next and previous tab in a horizontal list, wrapping at the ends and stepping over disabled tabs. Mirrored in a right-to-left page.
The same in a vertical list. The off-axis pair is left to the page, so a horizontal list does not eat a scroll.
Chooses the focused tab. Only `activation="manual"` needs them; automatic activation has already chosen it.

a11y: `role="tablist"` on the list, named by its own `label` — a page can hold several, and a tablist has no name of its own.
`role="tab"` with `aria-selected` on each tab, and `aria-controls` naming the panel it shows — written only while that panel is mounted, since a dangling reference names nothing.
`role="tabpanel"` on the panel, `aria-labelledby` its tab, and `tabindex="0"` so the content is reachable from the keyboard whether or not anything inside it is focusable.
`aria-orientation` follows `orientation`, and the arrows follow the reading order: in a right-to-left page ArrowLeft is the *next* tab.
